title: Optimal quantum query complexity of uniformity testing
formal: Determine \(Q(d,\varepsilon )\), the optimal worst-case quantum query complexity of distinguishing \(p=u_{d}\) from \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p,u_{d})>\varepsilon\) with success probability at least 0.99, up to universal constant factors jointly for all integers \(d\ge 2\) and real \(0<\varepsilon \le 1/4\). Access is to an arbitrary distribution synthesizer with the precise oracle convention below.
context:
Ordinary sample access reveals only independent outcomes. Coherent access to a sampler and its inverse permits interference between executions. This can reduce the number of calls needed to detect a departure from uniformity; a classical sample lower bound therefore does not automatically apply.

The paper establishes \(O(\min \{d^{1/3}/\varepsilon ^{4/3},\sqrt{d}/\varepsilon\})\) queries. The terms cross at \(\varepsilon =d^{-1/2}\): the first governs larger errors and the second smaller errors. The question asks whether any quantum tester can improve this full dependence.

The source recalls \(\Omega (d^{1/3})\) queries for constant \(\varepsilon\) and \(\Omega (1/\varepsilon )\) already on a two-element domain. Knowing both separately does not yield their conjectured joint dependence. For example, at \(\varepsilon =d^{-1/2}\) the target is \(\Omega (d)\).

For a string \(x\in [d]^{m}\), the standard oracle maps |\(j,z\rangle\) to |\(j,z\oplus x_{j}\rangle\) and defines \(p_{i}=|\{j:x_{j}=i\}|/m\). The authors also conjecture the same lower bound even with this structure available, in the worst case over m and x. This is a stronger claim than the arbitrary-synthesizer target selected here; fixed small m can cap the cost through reading the entire string.

The original conjecture predicts \(Q(d,\varepsilon )=\Theta (\min \{d^{1/3}\varepsilon ^{- 4/3},d^{1/2}\varepsilon ^{- 1}\})\), with its upper bound proved by the source. The retained target asks for the optimal joint function even if that candidate lower bound is false; it is not asserted to be logically equivalent to the conjecture.
why: Would identify the optimal joint dependence on domain size and accuracy for one of the basic distribution-testing tasks with coherent sampler access, clarifying the extent of quantum advantage over classical samples.
status_note: Conjecture, access definitions, version record and later-result searches checked through 12 September 2026. No matching general quantum-query lower bound was located; classical uniformity and quantum-state measurement results use different access models.

progress.text: The TQC paper supplies the matching candidate upper bound and states its optimality as Conjecture 2.

sentences: Uniformity testing distinguishes a perfectly uniform distribution from one separated in total variation distance.
The tester can coherently call a unitary preparing the distribution, its inverse and its controlled version.
Its guarantee must hold for arbitrary garbage states and arbitrary valid unitary extensions.
The target is the optimal query count jointly in domain size and distance, up to universal factors.
The source supplies a candidate upper bound whose matching lower bound remains conjectural.

references.title: Uniformity Testing When You Have the Source Code
references.authors: Canonne, Clément L.; Kothari, Robin; O'Donnell, Ryan

definitions: Write \([d]=\{1,\ldots ,d\}, u_{d}(i)=1/d\) and \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p,u_{d})=(1/2)\sum_{i}|p_{i}- 1/d|\). The algorithm receives d and \(\varepsilon\) and oracle access to a unitary \(U_{p}\) satisfying \(U_{p}|0^{k}\rangle =\sum_{i}\sqrt{p_{i}}|i\rangle |\psi _{i}\rangle\), where each garbage state |\(\psi _{i}\rangle\) is normalized. The extension of \(U_{p}\) away from |\(0^{k}\rangle\) and its garbage states are arbitrary; the tester must work for every valid oracle satisfying the promise. A query is one application of \(U_{p}, U_{p}\dagger\) or controlled-\(U_{p}\); intervening quantum operations, ancillas and measurements are unrestricted and do not count toward query complexity. The code is used as a black box: the tester does not get a classical description to inspect for free. Let \(Q(d,\varepsilon )\) be the minimum worst-case number of such queries among testers whose probability of the correct yes/no output is at least 0.99 for every oracle with \(p=u_{d}\) or \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p,u_{d})>\varepsilon\), taking the worst case over allowed oracle-register sizes. No guarantee is required in the intermediate gap.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function \(g(d,\varepsilon )\) and absolute constants \(a,A>0\) such that a \(g(d,\varepsilon )\le Q(d,\varepsilon )\le A g(d,\varepsilon )\) throughout the stated domain. Prove both bounds uniformly over its two parameters and all valid oracle implementations. A formula or certified evaluation rule may specify g; merely renaming Q is insufficient. This is an asymptotic query bound up to multiplicative constants, not pointwise additive 0.01 accuracy.
